prediction.likelyOutcome: Huntington should obtain judgment and foreclosure on both properties for the reinstated cognovit judgment amount plus accruing interest, late charges and contractual attorney fees, and should retain the Central Avenue sale proceeds and the great majority of the disputed insurance proceeds; Limited's breach-of-contract and fraud counterclaims are unlikely to succeed given its own failure to submit required draw documentation, though its conversion claim over the unilaterally-endorsed insurance check creates a real, if probably manageable, risk of a partial offset.

outcome.description: After a January 2017 bench trial the court entered judgment for Huntington in all four actions, rejected the borrower's claims, held the cognovit judgment could not be collaterally attacked and that Huntington was entitled to recover the full amount of the cognovit note, $1,374,413.88 (per diem $97.69733), and later awarded Huntington $928,593.73 in attorney fees and expenses. The Tenth District affirmed.
